records.c: M9 map strip: 64 cells, one per world column, read as $0600,Y by resident $4173 and $3B51 (the map repeats through mask $3F). The low nibble of a cell selects its block type through the table at $073E. Columns 0 to 3 hold 00 01 02 03; the rest of the strip is zero.
192 bytes ($0640-$06FF) after the 64-cell strip, all zero. The map position is masked with $3F, so the scene never indexes these bytes.

Start of the 32-byte scene header that the loader at $557A unpacks after the map. The bytes are $50 39 2D 2D 01 00 00 00 0B 0D 0D 0D 0D 0D 55 39. The loader reads $0701 ($39, "9") as the name character of the picture P and character set C resources it loads to $BC00 and $E000, $070F ($39, "9") as the name character of the overlay U loaded to $8B00, and $0703 ($2D, "-") as the extra costume selector, where a dash means none. $0700 and $0702 are not read by the loader.

Three numeric header bytes: $0704 (1) is the loop limit the loader compares at $568F and is read by the camera and motion routines, $0705 (0) indexes the tables at $59A1 and $59A8 that set $5E, $5F and $60, and $0706 (0) is halved into $02C8 and $02C7 at $566A.

Seven colour bytes ($0707-$070D = 00 0B 0D 0D 0D 0D 0D) read by $5A34: $0708 and $0709 go to the VIC background colour registers $D022 and $D023, $0707 is cached at $02DD as the display colour, and $070A-$070D are copied to the four message palette bytes $6998-$699B.
Two bytes, "U9" ($55 $39): the overlay resource name, whose second character the loader compares with its cache at $508E and loads at $8B00 ($070F).

Ten bytes ($0710-$0719 = 00 10 21 32 3C 4A 60 00 FA F8): depth thresholds. $0710 is read by the object grid and placement routines ($37B4, $383F, $5487), $0711 at $548A, $0718 at $5397 and $0719 at $53B9.

Costume selector ($05), the index into the initial-animation table at $5985 read at $51EA and $5985. The three bytes after it ($071B-$071D = FF 37 FF) are read at $5201, $5207 and $51E4 when entry placement starts.
Sixteen replacement cell nibbles for OPEN, indexed by the current cell's low nibble. Bytes: 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0A 0B 0C 0D 0E 0F. Nibbles that change: none.
Sixteen replacement cell nibbles for CLOSE, indexed by the current cell's low nibble. Bytes: 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0A 0B 0C 0D 0E 0F. Nibbles that change: none.

Sixteen low-nibble-to-type values read by $4171/$4173 and $3B51 (bytes: 0F 0F 0F 0F 01 01 01 01 01 01 01 01 01 01 01 01). Types $80 and above are negative; the engine falls back to depth-table index zero for them.

Sixteen inclusive upper column bounds read by $4115 (bytes: FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF). Resident $411C takes the first entry whose bound is at least the coarse column, so each region is the span of columns up to its bound.

Sixteen bytes ($075E-$076D) after the column thresholds. In this scene the sequence code uses $075E-$0766 as per-cell step counters (wise_mark_current_cell sets one to 1, wise_reset_cells clears them), so they are live data, not padding; the exit scan at $411C stops at index 15 ($075D) and does not read them.

Sixteen source selectors, one per region (bytes: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00). Resident $412B reads the one for the region found at $411C: 0 uses the region itself as the table index (bank 0), 1 takes bits $60 of the state byte $0500, 2 takes bits $60 of $0501, and 3 or more take bits $60 of the shared PRNG. The selected bank (0 to 3) is offset 32 bytes per bank into the exit arrays.

Called every frame by wise_update while wise_sequence_step ($8D37) is not negative. Branches on its value 0 to 7 to the step routines below (0 to $9112, 1 to $9131, 2 to $9136, 3 to $9159, 4 to $917D, 5 to $919D, 6 to $9210, 7 to $9223); any other value returns. Each step watches the per-cell counters $075E-$0766 that the resident special-cell routine fills as the player steps on cells 0 to 8, and opens an exit through $922E. What the cells look like on screen is not identified here.

Step 0. Counts the nonzero counters among cells 0 to 2 ($075E-$0760). Returns unless at least two are nonzero. Then scans cells 2, 1, 0 for the first zero counter and opens the exit there through $922E; returns if all three are nonzero.
Step 1. Opens the exit of cell 2 at once through $922E (Y=2), every frame it is called.
Step 2. Like step 0 for cells 6 to 8 ($0764-$0766): returns unless at least two counters are nonzero, then opens the exit through $922E at the first cell, scanning 6 up to 8, whose counter is zero.

Step 3. Calls $923B (returns from here if no counter changed). Compares $0372, the current cell, with the stored last cell $8D3C and stores it. If the cell changed: resets with $9253 and marks the new cell with $926C. If unchanged and the cell is 6 to 8 with its counter equal to 2: opens its exit through $922E.

Step 4. Same as step 3 but for any cell 0 to 8: after $923B, a changed cell resets the counters ($9253) and marks the new cell ($926C); the same cell with counter equal to 2 opens its exit through $922E.

Step 5. After $923B, saves the last cell $8D3C into $8D3F and stores $0372 in $8D3C. Counter sum below 2: returns. Sum equal to 2: if the new cell plus 1 (wrapping 9 to 0) is the previous cell, stores $FF in $8D3E; if the new cell minus 1 (wrapping) is the previous cell, stores 1; otherwise resets ($9253) and marks the cell ($926C). Larger sums continue at $91E0.

Step 5, sum above 2. If $8D3E is nonnegative, calls $9278 (new cell is previous plus 1) and returns. If negative: the previous cell must equal the new cell plus 1 (wrapping); on a match with sum 8 it opens the exit of the cell below the current one (0 wraps to 8) through $922E; a mismatch resets and marks the cell. So eight steps around the ring of cells 0 to 8 in one direction open the exit.
Step 6. After $923B, saves the last cell into $8D3F, stores $0372 in $8D3C and calls $9278: the walk must go up one cell at a time. Unlike step 5 it does not set a direction.
Step 7. If the cell 0 counter ($075E) is nonzero, opens the exit of cell 4 through $922E (Y=4). Otherwise returns.

Opens exit Y (a cell index 0 to 8). Stores wise_exit_entry ($8D3A) in the bank 0 exit entry table at $078E,Y and wise_exit_scene_request ($8D39) in the bank 0 scene request table at $077E,Y. The resident exit code ($4128) then sends the player to that scene when the cell is entered. Called from the step routines above.

Adds the nine counters $075E-$0766 (8-bit sum, returned in A) and compares it with the stored sum $8D3D. If equal, pops its return address and returns, so the calling step routine ends. Otherwise stores the sum in $8D3D and returns. Called by steps 3 to 6.

For cells 8 down to 0: clears the counter $075E,Y and the scene request $077E,Y, and copies the original entry id from $07AE,Y back to $078E,Y. Then clears $8D3E. Called by the step routines when a walk is broken, and by wise_ask_wise_man.
Sets the counter of the current cell ($075E indexed by $0372) to 1 and sets the counter sum $8D3D to 1, so the walk starts again from this cell.

Ring walk, upward direction. Takes Y = $0372 minus 1 (0 wraps to 8). If Y equals the previous cell $8D3F: with the counter sum in A equal to 8, opens the exit of the cell above the current one (8 wraps to 0) through $922E; with another sum, returns. If Y differs, resets ($9253) and marks the current cell ($926C). Called by steps 5 and 6.
